---
title: Local Projections in One Page
date: 2026-08-01
summary: The estimating equation, interpretation, and a minimal R specification for impulse responses.
tags:
  - Econometrics
  - Macroeconomics
  - R
---

For horizon $h$, a local projection estimates a separate regression

$$
y_{t+h}-y_{t-1}=\alpha_h+\beta_h\varepsilon_t+\Gamma_h'X_{t-1}+u_{t+h}.
$$

The sequence $\{\beta_h\}_{h=0}^H$ traces the response of $y$ to the identified shock $\varepsilon_t$. Each horizon is estimated directly, so misspecification does not compound through recursive iteration as it can in a VAR.

```r
horizons <- 0:12
irf <- lapply(horizons, function(h) {
  fit <- lm(dplyr::lead(y, h) - dplyr::lag(y) ~ shock + lags, data = df)
  coef(fit)[["shock"]]
})
```

## Identification remains the hard part

Local projections change the propagation estimator, not the source of exogenous variation. A causal interpretation of $\beta_h$ still requires a defensible shock, timing convention, and information set.

Standard errors must also reflect overlapping outcomes when $h>0$. In annual or quarterly macroeconomic applications, heteroskedasticity-and-autocorrelation robust inference is usually the minimum starting point.
